citations.context: So we're mainly focusing on problematic passages. So I already read you the first couple verses there. Let's just keep going through chapter one. In verse six, we get this. Who can stand before his indignation? Who can endure the heat of his anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are broken into pieces by him. The next sentence is the Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble. Again, in group and out group, speaking for the chosen people, God is slow to anger.

text.KJV: Who can stand before his indignation? and who can abide in the fierceness of his anger? his fury is poured out like fire, and the rocks are thrown down by him.
text.WEB: Who can stand before his indignation? Who can endure the fierceness of his anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are broken apart by him.

citations.context: Then at verse 10, we get desolate, desolation and ruin, hearts melt and knees tremble, anguish is in all loins, all faces grow pale. Remember that God is slow to anger, he is loving, he is steadfast in his life. And then verse 13, Behold, I am against you, declares the Lord of hosts, and I will burn your chariots in smoke, and the sword shall devour your young lions, I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers shall no longer be heard. Oh what a good God.
